newsitem.title: PERU: Peru mudslide kills 33, at least 100 missing.
newsitem.headline: Peru mudslide kills 33, at least 100 missing.

text.p: At least 33 people were killed and more than 100 were missing when an Andean mountainside collapsed on Tuesday in southeastern Peru, sending a wall of mud into two villages, destroying them, authorities said.
"We have recovered 33 bodies at this point. That is confirmed," Luis Barra Pacheco, mayor of the region's capital, Abancay, told Reuters. "Under the mud there are at least 100 people."
Darkness, heavy fog and further small landslides in the area prompted rescuers to call off the search for more victims at about 5 p.m EST (2200 GMT).
Civil defence workers, police, firefighters and Peruvian army units were slated to resume search efforts at dawn, the mayor's assistant, Julio Ocampo said.

Officials and firefighters returning from the scene in Apurimac department, some 380 miles (480 kms) southeast of Lima, said they had pulled dozens of bodies from the mud and had seen many mutilated corpses.

"There were arms, heads, pieces of bodies sticking out of the mud," firefighter Richard Rojas told Reuters by telephone after returning to Abancay. "We have tried to dig up the bodies using picks and shovels, but it's been difficult."
Rescuers said the corpses had been battered and mutilated by rocks carried in the torrent of mud.
The mudslide occurred at about 4 a.m. (0900 GMT), virtually burying the villages of Ccocha and Pumaranra, near Abancay, which were home to nearly 250 people.
"Two villages have totally disappeared," Barra Pacheco said, adding an estimated 10.5 million cubic feet (300,000 cubic metres) of mud slid off the mountain.

Police said the villages had been evacuated prior to the mudslide after weekend flooding. But their refuge in a fold of the mountain just above the villages put them squarely in the path of the mud as it tumbled down on Monday.
Area legislator Dennis Vargas Marin called on President Alberto Fujimori to declare a state of emergency.

"As a congressman, I ask that the city of Abancay and its surrounding districts be declared in a state of emergency," he told local radio. He estimated that up to 300 people may have disappeared and warned of more potential disasters if the seasonal torrential rains continued.

Fujimori met with his Cabinet in the afternoon to discuss the mudslide and the hostage crisis at the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence, where Marxist rebels were holding 72 hostages for the 63rd day.
The Civil Defence said it was sending 18 tons of supplies to the region for survivors, as well as three dogs to help find bodies and a geologist to assess further risks.

Police said reports from villagers indicated 50 to 60 families were buried. The mayor's office faxed a list to Reuters with the names of 134 villagers reported missing, among them entire families. But Abancay officials said the number of casualties was probably closer to 150 and 200.

Rescue workers prepared to evacuate more than 60 families on Wednesday from towns near the disaster zone to schools on the outskirts of Abancay, in case of further slides. Ccocha and Pumaranra are about six miles (10 kms) east of Abancay.
Alejandro Caballero, mayor of the neighbouring village of Tamburco, said he believed there were more than 200 people missing. "No one has survived there," he said.
Flash floods, mudslides and landslides are common in Peru's Andes during the January to March rainy season.

Over the weekend, five people died in flooding in Tamburco, while floods in the jungle province of Rioja destroyed the homes of 500 families and swept away a woman and two children in the village of Yuracyacu.
